body.text: The operator requested four GPUs on every next run and measured end-to-end throughput. The first continuation ended r0055 after 62.22M active interactions; 48.99M r0051 was the stronger checkpoint. R2 judgment and replay are r0053 and r0054. Start an eight-update throughput study from the 48.99M checkpoint on CUDA 0,1,2,3 with full 900-step episodes, the same 40% domain randomization, and no reward changes. Record active and total rate after optimisation on every update and time simulation control, physics, sensor, inference, reward, resets, optimisation and collectives on updates 3, 6 and 8. Compare to the earlier hold benchmark. Solve the dominant measured production cost first. Preserve the exact CPU gate and check station outcomes for changes that affect the GPU simulator.

Four-L40S full-horizon baseline work/ppo_profile_4gpu_baseline ran eight actual PPO updates. Throughput from cold setup to checkpoint was 45,464 active steps/s. Warm updates 3–8 delivered 58,301–66,543 active steps/s including optimiser and sync, median 63,610. CUDA events on each critical rank attributed 4.43–4.75 s to physics in a 10.26–11.21 s update, 0.81–1.47 s to reset, 1.19 s to arm control, 0.66–0.68 s to station sensor, about 0.13 s each to policy inference and history features, and 1.24–1.27 s to optimisation including 0.25–0.27 s gradient/statistics sync. Batch synchronisation also absorbs rollout load imbalance, reaching 0.73 s on rank zero. The r0039 hold workload neither contacts with the moving hand nor resets nor trains. Physics is the largest production cost. Measure maximum contact and constraint allocations on actual full-horizon PPO before decreasing the buffers, following the MuJoCo Warp performance documentation. Keep every candidate on station rules and the same CPU evaluator.

The four-L40S capacity baseline performed 16 full-horizon PPO updates in work/ppo_profile_4gpu_capacity. Cold setup through checkpoint averaged 48,463 active steps/s. Updates 3–16 had median 65,031 and range 27,238–71,552, including optimisation. The first 900-step group reset together and caused the low update, with 2,486 ended episodes and 17.78 s of collection. Across all sampled physics substeps the largest per-world constraint count was 148 under a limit of 420. Peak batch contacts on a rank were 19,999 under capacity 159,744, collision candidates peaked at 15,765 and the maximum solver iterations was 14; no structural capacity or cycle-limit flags. The matched next study reduces caps to 224 constraints and 65,536 batch contacts per rank, preserving major headroom and aborting on structural overflow. Each future throughput number names its actual workload and timing denominator.

The four-GPU measurement work/ppo_profile_4gpu_tight finished 16 updates at 50,744 active steps/s through startup, with a warm median 65,488 (baseline capacity audit 65,031). Per-rank constraints peaked at 143 of 224 and contacts peaked at 19,926 of 65,536. No capacity, solver-iteration or linesearch-limit flags. Contact memory fell from approximately 4.1 to 3.1 GB per GPU at comparable stages. The reset-heavy update improved from 27,238 to 33,143 active steps/s, with similar primary physics section times on profiled updates. This was a buffer-size change only. Test the reset refresh and later increase environments per GPU with headroom. Removing 63 visual-only geometries was independently checked on three CPU command replays, with exact generalized positions and visibility and no contact disagreements. It has not entered the performance study yet.

The four-GPU fast-reset study work/ppo_profile_4gpu_fast_reset used the smaller audited buffers and the original 2 ms physics. Its 16 updates averaged 55,915 active steps/s through setup and reached 71,080 warm median, versus 50,744 and 65,488 respectively with full refresh. The first reset-heavy update rose from 33,143 to 39,551 and the profiled reset region fell to 0.09–0.59 s on four ordinary sampled updates. The reset-only graph computes rigid transforms, contact and bias for the first servo update, leaving acceleration and constraints to the next ordinary mjw.step. In 48 randomized-backend worlds with 24 prepared starts, immediate generalized states, contact flags and geometry matched exactly, and servo bias/passive fields differed by at most 3.82e-6. The first action step differed in generalized position by 2.98e-7, with no differing contact flags. Separate GPU instances then diverged on contact by step eight (max generalized-position difference 0.0233, no stop or safety discrepancy). This is a local numerical diagnostic. The selected optimisation still needs paired outcome and station checks. All four GPUs are now testing 4,096 worlds each with unchanged 80-step rollouts and doubled local minibatches.

Four-L40S 16,384-world run work/ppo_profile_4gpu_large reached 19,735,332 active policy interactions in 214.11 s including setup (92,175/s). Updates 3–16 averaged 106,985 active steps/s end to end including the first reset burst. Median 116,258, range 65,925–121,355. The same 80-step rollout and doubled local 4,096 minibatch kept optimisation near 1.2 s/update. Physics remained largest at 5.49–6.02 s in ordinary profiles and 7.68 s during the reset-heavy contact update. Policy inference was about 0.135 s, sensor 0.65–0.70 s, arm 1.49 s, and reset refresh 0.37–0.82 s or 2.16 s in the burst. The caps heard peak 165/224 constraints and 39,584/131,072 batched contacts with zero overflow. The official accelerated GPU station check had 13 passes and the prior explained finger-speed warning. Two independent 128-start CPU comparisons passed official outcome parity. Legacy GPU 10 vs CPU 14 hardware violations and zero lift, drop, success both. On r0051 actor CPU 120 lift/8 turn/128 drop/2 unsafe vs accelerated GPU 117/4/127/0, and original GPU 121/6/128/4. No carries or full successes in these policy comparisons. Four matched feasibility commands gave GPU 4 lift, 2 turn, 1 carry and 0 successful seats, with no stops or violations. CPU 4/4/3/3. The speed configuration is ready for the final contract-training audit. The exact frozen evaluator stays in place.

simulator.name: MuJoCo

backends.training: MuJoCo Warp 3.17.0 on four NVIDIA L40S GPUs, 4096 worlds per GPU. The arm and hand run at 100 Hz, rigid-body substeps are 2 ms, and the outer policy and object estimator use 30 Hz.

simulator.training_reset: After a physical reset, refresh kinematics, contact and servo bias in a CUDA graph. Normal physics solves acceleration and constraints before integration. Audit structural capacity at each 2 ms substep and abort training if any GPU has truncated physics buffers.

scene.robot: Complete supplied Marvin–Wuji MJCF with official arm capsules and hand collision meshes, the parked left arm and the column and head stop volumes. Added table, pedestal and floor. The geometric station stops are evaluated directly on commanded and measured arm angles.
scene.object: Rounded convex 27 × 40 × 43 mm housing and two separated 6 × 1.5 × 15 mm blade boxes. Only the deployed white object is instantiated.

object_physical_properties.dominant_material: molded thermoplastic housing, plated metal blades

sources.mass_kg: Comparable Anker and Belkin 20 W adapters span 36–52 g (https://www.anker.com/products/b2348112-f0 and https://www.belkin.com/support-article/?articleNum=337529). Adopt 51 g for the larger housing.
sources.com_m: Homogeneous housing with heavier internal assembly offset 2 mm toward the back and two exterior brass blade cuboids.
sources.inertia_com_kgm2: Parallel-axis combination of housing and blade cuboids about the inferred combined COM.
sources.friction: Assumed effective coefficients for molded polymer against smooth laminate. Measure and randomize for robot deployment.
sources.restitution: Assumed 0.05, weak bounce of molded plastic on a rigid table; not identifiable from the clip.
sources.dominant_material: Appearance and construction class suggest a stiff molded thermoplastic with plated metal blades. Resin and alloy unobservable.
sources.size_m: TASK_CONFIG.md section 3 dimensions for the visually matching station adapter. Industrial design is consistent with the white Type A Apple 20 W USB-C form in https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mwvv3am/a/20w-usb-c-power-adapter. Brand identity is unconfirmed.

reference.source: Reconstruction version 6, right MANO wrist, plug_white world pose, phase annotations and object-frame contact witnesses.
reference.kinematic_replay: Align the opening blade direction to deployment yaw about the tabletop normal. Offset to the fixed start and gradually bring the endpoint to the center of the goal. Apply measured wrist rotations relative to the grasp wrist, which is anchored in the reachable robot hand frame from an opposed thumb–middle-finger pad solve. Re-solve the pad locations and the arm IK per frame. Choose the smallest collision-clear separation available at each frame. Keep the measured plug trajectory as an imposed pose for the kinematic audit.
reference.planned_reward_reference: Adapt the demonstrated object and wrist traces to each start and goal. Use object position, blade-axis rotation, wrist tracking, opposed-contact witnesses and ordered state-dependent progress. Keep the reconstruction in the reward and curriculum.

arm.controller: Public 100 Hz palm jump test, linear and rotational slew, box clamp, measured-joint seeded IK, coupled wrist and command speed clamps. Delayed position reference followed by an implicit, current-limited arm joint servo. Command and measured capsules are evaluated each tick.
arm.numerical_limit: The public reference integrator occasionally advances its feed-forward component past the IK boundary. Project the resulting joint reference to the same joint and coupled wrist box and clear outward velocity at a projected joint, consistent with the published lack of boundary overshoot. The unreachable-orientation test then passes.
arm.initialization_correction: Target replay r0034 showed that re-solving Cartesian IK at the placed palm during the ramp changed the arm null-space posture by 9.53 degrees. Joint hold reproduced all eight observed no-lift outcomes and reduced the median valid-state position residual from 334 mm to 53 mm. The remaining post-start Cartesian and arm servo law is the same.

hand.controller: Five ordered four-joint digits, 2 Hz first-order filter, 25 ms nominal fractional delay, torque-limited implicit position servo and compliant joint stops. Measured hand positions are delayed and receive 0.10 degree encoder noise.
hand.domain_randomization: Draw nominal or randomized strength, delay, friction, object inertia/mass, table edges and stop compliance. Nominal values are used in the frozen evaluation. The sampled distributions for each training run are recorded with its iteration.
hand.stop_distributions: Use .001–.010 rad sampled uniformly on randomized episodes, converted to max(.004, .006 × sqrt(compliance/.002)) for the constraint time constant while retaining the nominal damping ratio and deployed limits. The nominal compliant-stop setting remains .002 rad.

sensor.source: Published d2s_sensor.PoseSensor for delay, symmetry flips, noise, loss and validity/age. Contact-mesh-derived capsules approximate ego occlusion; sample 112 physical housing surface points and 12 blade face points. Recompute visibility at each physics-log tick.
sensor.encoder_delay: Normal 14 ms with 4.3 ms deviation, clipped to 4–29 ms and sampled on the logged 100 Hz trajectory.
sensor.training_backend: Published TorchPoseSensorBatch with the same default noise, delays and occlusion schedule, using the same 124 samples and arm or hand capsule rays in Warp. CPU and GPU use independently seeded noise streams.

initial_conditions.object: Uniform and independent xy offsets ±10 mm, yaw offset ±10 degrees about -90 degrees, state +X upward. Place with zero velocities on the table and verify support with the installed hold check. Use the published start IK and 1.5 s hand ramp.
initial_conditions.arm_ramp: Solve the package start once from the published reset joints. Keep those placed joint references for all 150 finger ramp ticks while gravity, finger dynamics, collisions and the pose sensor advance. No Cartesian IK iterations run the warm arm reference. At t=0, compare the first action with the measured palm. Local arm variation was at most 2.18e-5 rad over the ramp, and the final joint vector differs from target [redacted] by at most 1.63e-6 rad.
initial_conditions.training: GPU PPO uses the same simulated 1.5-second deployment ramp on each complete reset. Optional intermediate-state starts restore the position, velocity and hand preload of a mechanically settled pose. The fixture used during offline initialization is gone before the saved states. No controller commands enter the network training targets.

episode.termination: Published geometric and jump stops and invalid action or nonfinite state as policy failure. Finger and arm travel violations are logged without turning contact force into a stop.

station_check.departure: Index MCP1 finite-difference peak 10.105 rad/s on CPU and 10.106 on GPU, above the 8.203 rad/s model value and below the public 2 Hz-filtered-step limit 22.117 rad/s. No stop or measured excess travel in the check. The hardware spec leaves the interpretation of the quantized peak open.

validation.fk: Compared MuJoCo palm FK to the arm model at reset (about 4 micrometres); station adapter passes published free-space, limit and stop checks.
validation.sensor_replay: Four independent 900-step lock-ramp candidate state logs reproduced contract-v3 sensor observations and all other checks with zero discrepancies.
validation.initial_hold: All 128 deployment evaluations retained the intended joint hold during the finger ramp and started the actor without a station stop. A full gate start check on the frozen v3 evaluator will verify the support convention.
validation.rollout_penetration: Kinematic reference maximum 0.992 mm. The maximum signed hand–plug overlap on the 128 CPU corrected-ramp neural rollouts is 3.88 mm. Early impacts can press the current estimated compliance more deeply than the kinematic replay. The current actor is a baseline and poses a finger travel risk in contact.
limitations: Mass, friction and inertia remain priors pending target calibration. Geometry treats blade holes and rear electrical recess as closed collision surfaces.

Capsules approximate partial occlusion by the glove. Finger pads are compliant contact surfaces over rigid links. The kinematic replay deviates up to 32 mm from the unconstrained palm placement and comes within 5 mm of the plug in 50 of 76 grasp frames. The reconstruction wrist and object remain the demonstration targets.

The target, nominal replay and corrected replay had median per-trial peak external torques of 89.95, 28.03 and 32.39 Nm. This is an estimated observation. Target finger excursions beyond the deployed travel allowance occurred in eight of eight; the corrected sent-command replay reproduced them in three of eight. Continue calibration using outcomes and uncertainty, not exact occluded trajectories.

parity.limitation: No complete neural episodes on these checkpoints. Stage counts are shown in addition to the official tolerances.

throughput.timing: Real rollout, reward, resets, policy inference, gradients and synchronization counted, with capacity and contract checks enabled.

validation.target_replay: R2 r0054 reproduced four lifts and seven measured finger-range violations with joint calibration at 0.1075 s arm delay and 0.010 rad compliant-stop parameter. Nominal yielded seven lifts and zero violations. The target had four visible lifts and eight measured violations. Preserve the remaining contact and pose uncertainty instead of identifying the target from a single fitted trajectory.
validation.dynamic_contact_diagnostic: Four matched task-feasibility command histories. GPU 4 lift, 2 turn, 1 carry, 0 place, versus CPU 4/4/3/3. No GPU stops or safety or capacity violations. The exact CPU judge remains the reference for learning carry into the low seated grasp.
validation.contract_in_training: All GPU worlds enforce finite actions/state, the station controller feedback and stops, measured finger and arm limits, and measured palm workspace and speed. One complete stream per rank feeds the installed ContractMonitor every controller row and policy step. The sampled episode ends when that monitor finds a problem. Full 900-step episodes are used throughout. The exact gate checks all policy episodes.

media.comparison_context: The visual reference replay is unchanged from earlier simulation versions. The improvements change the GPU training implementation and its uncertain-physics distribution.

body.frozen_evaluator: Task suite v3 r0036 and feasibility r0037 retain the identical nominal exact CPU evaluator.
body.training_domain_parameters_description: Nominal 60%. The general uniform ranges apply on 25%. The remaining 15% also uses those uncertainty ranges, with arm delay and compliant-stop softness sampled from the measured subranges below.

training_target_stratum.evidence: Round-two physical response timing and frequency of grip and encoder outcomes, replay r0054.
training_target_stratum.sampling: Independent uniforms for the two changed quantities conditional on a common stratum.

gate_evidence.seen: r0045: In seed 18712140 the housing is briefly pinched near 0.46 s, then the wrist retreats empty by 4.38 s without turning. R2 command replay r0054 supports extra arm lag and compliant-stop sampling before training toward a longer maintained grip.

body.text: Resume the same PPO weights, value head and optimizer from the best 48.99M checkpoint in r0051, with all four L40S GPUs, 4096 worlds per GPU, 80-step rollouts, 4096 local minibatches and 900-step full episodes. Plan 52 minutes and distinguish full deployed starts from prepared suffix starts. Keep the existing reward and reset bank while turns first appear. In addition to the documented full horizon and throughput changes, give 15% of all episodes the jointly plausible arm-delay/stop-compliance ranges measured through R2 command replay r0054. Keep 60% nominal objects and dynamics, and 25% generic randomized dynamics. Hypothesis: enough interaction and continued contact with slower, more compliant starts increase learned valid turns and reduce unsafe near-table closing. Gate later checkpoints against the same CPU evaluator. Archive the full optimizer and fixed-start criteria, contract checks and representative three-view rollout at each evaluated checkpoint.

Separate carry-handoff diagnostic on the r0051 checkpoint while the recorded r0063 run continues unchanged. From the 20 prepared carry states the actor advanced the training carry criterion in 18 and reached the release target in two. On the five qualifying full-start turns, the closest prepared carry state was 105–139 mm away in the world. The plug was occluded throughout the actual handoffs and slipped within 0.14–0.29 s. On 12 paired, reachable states with initial opposition preserved, translating the whole grip to object height -0.172 m and y -0.176 m reduced carry advancement from 10 to 2. Both translations preserve the initial hand–plug geometry by solving the wrist IK. This is a prepared-start diagnosis, not a new task result. If carries remain absent after turns improve, add physically settled early-carry states sampled near the actual handoff and check that the actor learns to maintain the grip through that region. Keep the current 52-minute block unchanged while its checkpoints are measured. Artifacts: work/ppo_gpu_02_fourth_suffix.json, work/carry_entry_diagnostic.json and work/carry_shift_diagnostic.json.

body.reflection: The first full-horizon, four-GPU PPO continuation checkpoint at 38,987,204 new active steps had 45 lifts, five measured turns (four also pass the separate standard lift predicate), no carries or placements, 20 final rests, zero stops and three hardware violations on 64 fixed exact CPU starts. All five turning trials stayed within hardware limits. The parent r0051 had 61 lifts and five turns, 13 final rests and two hardware violations. The paired lift regression is 3 new versus 19 lost, one-sided exact p = 0.00043. The five turns are different sampled starts. The currently accepted r0045 had 52 lifts and no turns on this local set. Candidate package validation passed at 0.258 ms p99. The representative seed 79431 shows a measured turn and retained final robot rest, without a successful carry. Continue the recorded 52-minute study and retain the incumbent pending stronger fixed-start evidence. The early output provides no evidence of full skill mastery or target transfer.

body.text: The r0065 checkpoint retains a five-trial turn signal but still has no carry. In those runs the plug estimate is invalid when upright and unsupported contact ends 0.07–0.42 s later, with the plug still 153–186 mm short of the goal. Viewed the exact rollout montage for seed 79431, where the turn is followed by loosening and drop. To probe the preceding transition, prepared 16 horizontal or nearly horizontal opposed pinches from 64 geometry trials without replaying any controls in the policy. Each retained state stayed at least 10 mm above the table with continuous opposed contact for 0.20 s after removing the temporary reset fixture. Starting tilt 78.9–90.4 degrees and no rotation credit. From these same states r0051 advanced the training turn condition on 2/16 and r0065 on 6/16, five gains and one loss, no stops or hardware violations. This is separate from fixed deployment gates. It supports a future early-turn starting-state bridge if full-start turns flatten. The running PPO configuration remains unchanged.

body.reflection: The second full-horizon evaluated checkpoint has 77,037,694 new interactions. It recorded 52 lifts and five staged turns on 64 fixed exact CPU starts. All five turning trials also passed the separate lift predicate and stayed inside the hardware limits. There were no carries, placements or successes, 15 final rests, zero stops, and two finger excursions of 0.02056 and 0.02223 rad. The first checkpoint had 45 lifts. The paired change is 12 gains and 5 losses, one-sided p = 0.0717. The warm 48.99M-step parent still has higher lift frequency, 61/64. Estimated pose was valid in 0/5 at the start of upright contact. Median remaining unsupported contact was 0.43 s. The package validated at 0.266 ms p99. The same training experiment continues. Retain gate r0045 as incumbent and keep this checkpoint for diagnosis. Present evidence does not establish safe carry or transfer.

body.reflection: At 115,300,482 new steps, 52/64 exact CPU starts had a qualifying lift, six also qualified for a turn, and none achieved the carry or later stages. The six turning trials stayed within hardware limits. Three other trials had finger excursions of 0.02015–0.03419 rad, with no stops and 18 final rests. Against the previous fixed-start checkpoint, the paired turn difference was 6 gains versus 5 losses, one-sided p = 0.500. After reaching an upright axis the median remaining unsupported contact was 0.79 s. Local package validation at 0.257 ms p99. No promotion. The scheduled training continues. An independently generated near-horizontal curriculum has 61 real-pinched configurations surviving the nominal and R2-bracket checks after restoration, ready to test if full-start turns remain scarce after more of the current curve.

body.text: Reward audit on 24 of the restored near-horizontal opposed states. Under constant palm and finger targets, 22/24 collected more than 0.10 of turn shaping (median 0.762) without advancing the stage. With a slow 36-degree wrist rotation and constant finger targets, all 24 collected shaping (median 2.795) and none advanced. Three showed over 10 degrees of blade tilt reduction with under 6 degrees of hand-relative rotation during contact and still earned 0.90–3.22 turn reward. The existing stage bonus rejects these motions, but dense shaping still pays wrist-dominated or passive progress. Before the next long method change, test a turn potential based on the blade tilt reduction attributable to a relative axis change in the current palm frame, gated by opposing contact and matching command/encoder changes. Verify that a stationary grip and wrist-only control score no turn progress, and score qualified active feasibility sequences as a positive control. Do not alter the running r0063 experiment. Its full-start internal turns increased again after about 100M and one reached the training carry state, so keep evaluating it as scheduled.

body.reflection: The fourth checkpoint at 154,444,355 new steps lifted in 63/64 and completed a qualifying turn in 11/64. Ten turning episodes also met every hardware bound. Overall there were three measured finger excursions between 0.02019 and 0.02075 rad, zero stops, 13 final rests, and no complete carries, placements or successes. The median unsupported grip lasted 0.67 s after upright tilt. Contract-v3 package validation passed at 0.257 ms p99. In the earlier gate r0045 montage seed 18712140 the housing was lifted briefly then released without the required turn. From no turns on the incumbent local fixed set and 52 lifts to 11 turns and 63 lifts, the improvement warrants a blinded turn-predicting gate. The observed safety failures are reported and the incumbent is unchanged unless the official paired gate accepts. The planned main run continues.

body.text: The prospective in-hand turn shaping uses the current palm orientation for both the previous and current hand-relative blade axes. This cancels a common world wrist rotation. It credits signed tilt reduction only while opposed across consecutive observations and while the contacting digits have both measured and commanded changes. The tested normalized potential is limited by both actual blade-up tilt and accumulated signed in-hand contribution. The replay check yielded zero prospective turn credit on all 48 fixed-target or wrist-only controls, and positive control potentials 0.518–0.961 on all 12 archived qualifying active turns, including four on the corrected station. The separate Torch implementation in training/gpu/turn_effect.py passed the positive, wrist-only and passive controls. It is not wired into the live trainer. Select the next isolated method change after the ongoing continuation and the official gate.

On 16 paired fixed starts using the measured round-two dynamics bracket (0.1075 s arm delay and 0.010 rad compliant-stop parameter), the delivered r0044 checkpoint gave 9 lifts, 0 turns and 15 hardware violations. The r0070 checkpoint gave 16 lifts and 8 turns and 16 hardware violations, no task successes or stops. Every r0070 first violation was ring MCP2, typically at 0.21 s, before any opposed pinch. Fourteen plugs were still on the table. The median peak excursion was 0.0347 rad. Replaying the exact saved configurations two 100 Hz ticks earlier shows ring contact with the plug on 13/16; subsequent states often show ring contact with the table. Targets remained within their prescribed limits. In an eight-seed 4 s pose diagnostic, positive initial ring MCP2 offsets of 0.08 and 0.16 rad lowered median peak excursion from 0.0372 to 0.0275 and 0.0265 rad. The larger offset left five of eight unsafe and cut turns from five to two. Keep the existing package start. These are diagnostics outside the nominal gate. The next safety hypothesis is to pay for avoiding the measured buildup of joint excursion before the hard stop, with the rule and threshold unchanged.

body.text: The full planned 52-minute, four-L40S r0063 continuation completed 274,132,104 new active interactions in 3,126.54 seconds. It averaged 87,679 end-to-end active steps/s including setup and 88,343 after the first two updates. The later reset-heavy workload is slower than the controlled r0062 warm average of 103,999; preserve the measured end-to-end rates. The corrected signed turn reward was tested on identical Warp rollouts from 16 hold, 16 wrist-only and 16 random-finger starting cases. Median turn rewards old versus new were 0.897 versus 0, 2.700 versus 0, and 1.919 versus 1.662, with no stage progression or safety violations in these probes. Random finger actuation sometimes really alters the relative blade axis. The positive archived controls retain the measured signal in r0071. On 21 right-side carry poses the older reset-registration condition advanced 4/21, and restoring a plausible stale on-table estimate advanced 0/21. Stale observations make the actual carry handoff harder. This is diagnostic and did not alter the training distribution. Next test only the corrected turn reward, keeping the original start pool and dynamics until its outcome is measured.

The prior 271.59M checkpoint has 48 turns and zero violations. Both had 48 safe turning trials. Prefer the earlier checkpoint for the next gate and as the research parent. The endpoint package validated at 0.282 ms p99. The four-GPU full run averaged 87,679 active steps/s with setup and 88,343 after the first two updates across 217 updates. body.text: Exploration saturation may be preventing the learner from sampling its own active turns often enough to learn the carry. All 26 latent log standard deviations reached the 0.8 upper clamp by the r0068 checkpoint and are still there, so the training stochastic standard deviation is 2.226. On 16 exact-station deploy starts the same r0079 actor reached the training turn milestone 16 times with its deterministic action, 13 times with either 0.35 or 0.65 latent noise SD and 4 times at the existing 2.226. Mean normalized command distortion at 2.226 was 0.650 per coordinate versus 0.305 at 0.65. On 16 early carry resets completion of the training carry milestone was 4, 1, 3 and 2 respectively; the carry-only conclusion is uncertain. No official nominal verdict uses those probes. See work/exploration_r0079.json. After reviewing the turn reward comparison and latest gate, test a fixed 0.65 rollout SD as a single PPO setting from the strongest retained parent. Preserve actor inputs, inference, PPO objective, station, reset bank and reward for the isolated comparison. Expect more sampled full-start turns, with KL still moving and no loss in exact task-suite safety. Keep a separate option to test the verified early carry bank if the post-turn failure remains.

Causal curriculum preparation only. The new bank preserves all 239 original states and adds 107 geometry-prepared early carry states and 17 states from exact CPU rollouts of r0079 on 64 independent collection-only deploy starts. The collection produced 47 qualifying turns, no carries and no hardware violations. Each saved state preserves the object, wrist, fingers and velocities, using a contact preload estimated from the previous finger targets for the 17 learner states. To qualify after reset, it independently retains opposed contact, tilt at most 25 degrees and clearance at least 10 mm across 0.20 s with no support, stops or hardware violations in nominal and the R2 delay/compliance bracket. No observation or action sequence is stored in the bank or given to the network. Those starts have median y minus 0.261 m and z minus 0.205 m. The 107 prepared states have median y minus 0.218 m and z minus 0.189 m. The 20 retained original carry starts have median y minus 0.061 m and z minus 0.247 m. Preparation artifacts work/early_carry_prepared_validated.diagnostic.json, work/early_carry_policy_validated.diagnostic.json and work/training_reset_pool_early_carry.json. No change to the current run.

Its first 32 include 32 lifts and 24 turns versus the incumbent r0077, with no carries. I opened both official failed montages. Seeds 771472647 and 1574852048 have fingers around the plug at 0.46 s and the plug separated on the tabletop by 4.38 s. A distinct 24-start sent-command intervention near the upright handoff preserved either the palm commands or finger commands. The original median unsupported held time was 0.61 s. Holding only the current finger target with the original palm trajectory extended the median to the 3.01 s test limit and 15 of 24 remained held beyond 2.9 s. Holding only the palm gave 0.62 s. Holding both also gave 3.01 s. `None` entered the goal; the best frozen-finger case retained a 44 mm margin and still needed continued leftward travel. There were zero stops or violations in all 96 diagnostic replays. This attributes much of the loss to changing finger targets after turn, with a separate insufficient carry trajectory. The intervention is diagnosis only and provides no policy or training actions. Evidence work/ppo_gpu_03_eval_seventh/handoff_control.json.

body.text: The existing carry potential clips to zero when horizontal error from the goal centre exceeds the demonstrated displacement from the episode start. At the first opposed unsupported upright instant in all 48 qualifying fixed r0079 starts, it therefore pays zero for any reduction in the first 36–126 mm of horizontal error, median 85 mm. Work/ppo_gpu_03_eval_seventh/carry_reward_deadzone.json computes the exact current reference length separately for each start. The measured median remaining grip lasts 0.63 s. Removing the flat part and initializing the stage potential to its measured entry value would give credit for real leftward movement immediately while opposed or held upright. This is a candidate separate reward experiment after the ongoing turn-reward and fixed-exploration comparisons. Correction about r0086: the single finger excursion was in the first 32-start batch, while the 64-start extension added no excursions. Final paired tallies were 96 lifts and 69 turns against r0077 with 91 lifts and 35 turns. No carry or full success.

Operator-directed throughput continuation. The causal-turn run reached 91,765,539 active steps on four L40S in 18 minutes. Profiled early median physics was 5.67 s per rank per update and later contact-heavy profiles are larger; optimisation was 1.28 s including 0.26 s synchronization and inference 0.14 s. While the exact endpoint is rated, compare 6,144 worlds per GPU to the 4,096-world production configuration with the same checkpoint, seed, physical station, reward, dynamics, history, batch length and local minibatch. Measure sixteen real PPO updates, including initial 900-step reset bursts, and profile each update. The comparison is a throughput study; the exported state is not selected for the next policy. The target, exact CPU model, suite and hardware tolerances are unchanged. I inspected both latest causal gate failure montages: seeds 456244624 and 1119768816 are separated by 4.38 s after the plug was in the fingers at 0.46 s. The latter plug is upright outside the goal afterwards.

The accepted package is contract v3 and carries no assumption of task completion. The throughput-only probe and the already recorded exploration comparison do not use unseen [redacted] feedback. Four other starts exceeded arm joint-2 travel after the plug was already separated, from 7.73–25.09 seconds, and there were no stops. Nine final rests and zero placements or full successes. p99 local action time 0.255 ms. The accepted gate r0091 is the earlier first causal checkpoint. body.text: Continue the original causal-reward PPO lineage for another sustained block. At r0093 the number of exact full-start carries rose from zero to seven, all hardware-safe on those carrying starts. No seat or placement. Entry clearance was 152–182 mm, and the first subsequent separation occurred with at least 163 mm clearance; all seven lost the plug before it touched the support. Four other episodes exceeded arm joint 2 by a peak 1.004–1.072 degrees outside its IK range against a 1-degree evaluator allowance. Those events were 7.73–25.09 seconds into deployment, long after the last contact at 1.41–1.46 seconds. See work/ppo_gpu_04_causal_eval_final/postcarry_and_arm.json. Retain the r0093 network and optimizer for research continuation. Use the same causal reward, full horizon, physical distribution, reset bank and exploration while carry performance is still moving. Select world count using the independent r0090 timing study. The fixed-noise and carry reward ideas remain separate controls. r0091 is the current dev incumbent and has been sent as s03; this preplanned comparison makes no use of pending target feedback.

Use 6,144 worlds per GPU for the r0094 continuation. The matched 16-update PPO throughput study raised active rate after two warm-up updates from 102,117 to 129,337 steps/s across the same four L40S. Inclusive rate rose from 88,803 to 112,876. The first concentrated 900-step reset update rose from 63,297 to 82,873. Median per-rank physics time on matched profiled updates grew from 5.67 to 6.88 seconds while world count grew 50 percent, lowering physics cost per simulated world. Controller 1.74 s, sensor 0.70 s, inference 0.14 s, resets 1.02 s and optimiser 1.82 s including 0.34 s CUDA synchronization per profiled rank-update at the new size. All four devices ran concurrently, maximum observed 159 constraints and 87,683 contacts per rank batch, zero buffer overflows and no problems in five completed sampled contract audit streams. Dossier work/throughput/ppo_6144_real_comparison.json. These are short real-PPO measurements. Measure sustained throughput during the continuing contact-rich experiment too. Use sim v4 and the unchanged exact gate. First phase-4 training-style suffix diagnosis advances 3/24 on the 26 new high preseat states versus 12/19 near-table legacy states. Use the original bank in this continuation while full-start carries are emerging.

Seating is largely outside the present suffix distribution. r0093 accelerated toward the goal 152–182 mm above support, and all seven carriers lost contact before support. Each pose estimate was invalid throughout the measured held interval after entry, aged 1.10–1.26 s and showing 271–305 mm position error at entry. The present seat-height shaping score has negligible slope there: the height contribution to the normalized potential was at most 2e-17 on entry. Only 3 of 24 independently prepared high-seat suffixes reached the internal seat milestone, compared with 12 of 19 legacy near-table suffixes. See work/ppo_gpu_04_causal_eval_final/seat_entry_visibility_and_shaping.json and work/early_seat_pilot_r0093.json. Candidate next changes, after judging the ongoing continuation, are broadening only the preseat reset clearance or giving real lowering progress credit over the larger height. Occlusion remains a related observability limitation. Do not feed simulator state to the actor or reconfigure the frozen gate.

Paired high-seat suffix sensor intervention with unchanged r0093 actor and 26 physically validated starts. With the regular model reset, one of 26 estimates was initially registered, three advanced and one settled. Using a physically plausible stale tabletop cache aged about 0.8 s, one advanced and none settled. Neither sensor-model group had stops or hardware violations. As a privileged diagnostic, feeding live true object poses instead produced zero advances and 17 hardware violations. Fresh poses are out of the actor’s learned distribution in this phase. body.text: The latest fixed-start turn regression from r0091 52/64 to r0099 25/64 is a break in continuous opposed grip across lift to upright. r0099 reaches 25 degrees or less while unsupported and opposed at some point in all 64 starts, but only 25 retain the qualifying horizontal lift in that same continuous opposed interval. Every one of those 25 then passes the relative axis, wrist arc, passive turn and independent standard criteria. r0091 had 61 opposed upright instants and 52 uninterrupted intervals; r0093 had 63 and 40. Evidence work/turn_regression_causal_r0099.json. Current training can preserve its turn phase and carry progress across a short contact interruption, so a future reward study should tie post-lift turn eligibility and bonuses to the same supported-to-airborne opposed interval. Keep the exact evaluator and PPO actor interface unchanged. Current continuation remains on its scheduled run.

The continuous-grip diagnosis is sensitive to logging rate. Applying the custom verification to the saved r0099 state streams sampled at policy times gives 38 apparent turns versus 25 with the full controller-rate logs. Seventeen starts turn only in the subsampled view and four only in the full view. This compares two diagnostic sample rates and does not replace the gate. Future training alignment should latch opposition on 100 Hz controller ticks rather than read contact only at 30 Hz. Results work/ppo_gpu_05_causal_eval_02/continuous_grip_sampling.json.

body.next: Replay all eight complete 900-command streams. Compare the arm and early finger travel, supported and unsupported contact outcomes, estimator occlusion and final placement under nominal dynamics and the [redacted]-two bracket.

body.observation_mismatch: Every trial ran all 900 sent commands. All eight lost the object estimate during in-hand manipulation, with first losses starting 0.40–0.80 s and reacquisition at 2.77–5.03 s. Each had 16 valid final-half-second rows. The earlier arm placement mismatch remains resolved: the median initial palm-position discrepancy was below 0.001 mm using the locked ramp. Against nominal replay, early 0–0.28 s palm motion aligned best with 17.5–18.75 ms extra target lag, compared with about 22.5 ms in R2. On valid object rows the nominal median of within-trial pose errors was 104 mm and 100.5 degrees modulo blade-axis symmetry. The median is dominated by largely stationary observations after reacquisition and cannot establish the object motion during occlusion.
body.dynamics_mismatch: All eight target video sets visibly show an unsupported lift, and the operator reports six upright turns. `None` establishes the full measured active continuous-opposition criterion through estimator loss. All eight fail placement. Trial 2 ends standing with blade tilt 0.7 degrees and y = 0.0026 m, outside the goal. Nominal exact replay lifts eight and passes the turn criterion on six, with different identities from the operator reports. It has no carry or place, no stop and zero measured finger excursions. The target had eight excursions, median 0.109 rad, range 0.033–0.129 rad, while sent commands stayed inside the limits. Seven peak on lower ring MCP2 and one on index MCP1. First over-tolerance readings are at 0.30–0.333 s, before the main visible lift. Nominal replay median finger peak is 0.0070 rad. Median recorded peak external torque estimate was 70.1 Nm versus 21.7 Nm in nominal replay. Torque is an estimated station channel, not a measured contact load. The R2 bracket at arm delay 0.1075 s and compliance parameter 0.010 gives eight lifts, five turns and six excursions. Keeping that arm delay and testing 0.022 and 0.038 gives eight lifts and eight excursions each, with seven and five turns respectively. Their median peaks are 0.026 and 0.041 rad, still below the target; the latter maximum is 0.077 rad. Testing only compliance 0.022 at nominal arm delay gives eight lifts, six turns and six excursions. `None` of these replays incurs a stop or completes a placement.
body.changes: Retain the exact frozen nominal judge, arm placement and hardware thresholds. The same early lag persists across two rounds, supporting the existing arm-delay stratum. The R3 replay supports broader training uncertainty for measured finger stop response, especially approaching the 0.022 setting, because it captures excursion frequency while preserving lift frequency. It does not identify actual compliance or reproduce the observed magnitudes. Treat it as a next isolated robustness experiment after the scheduled continuation and compare on both nominal and target-bracket starts. The uploaded logs are the unmodified nominal CPU replays of the exact sent commands. The four variant logs and the alignment measurements remain in work/[redacted]/.

body.success_rule: every stage, at rest over the last 0.5 s (finger joint range <= 0.05 rad, palm range <= 0.005 m), hardware within limits, no stop
body.reason: 'carry' better on the same seeds: 16 episodes only the candidate completes vs 0 only the incumbent (sign test p = 1.5e-05 <= 0.05); no stage significantly worse; hardware violations 0 vs 1

body.text: Fresh r0106 accepted the sustained causal PPO checkpoint r0102 under unchanged task suite v3. It records 32 lifts, 24 qualifying turns, 16 held carries, zero place/success and zero hardware violations. Paired carry gains 16 versus no losses, p=0.000015. I opened both actual failed montages, seeds 1670654587 and 1553138275. They have the plug near the fingers at 0.46 s and flat on the table away from the empty hand by 4.38 s. On 25 fixed local carries there is 83–143 mm clearance at goal entry and median 0.73 s additional held time. All separate airborne and all have an invalid estimate at entry. In the separate R3 calibration bracket of 0.1075 s and 0.022 rad, r0102 shows 16 lifts, 11 turns, 10 carries and 14/16 hardware violations, with one safe carry. r0091 shows 15 lifts, 8 turns, no carries and 13/16 excursions on the same starts. The latest target had excursions in all eight, and this comparison has unresolved transfer. Keep the next target round available while testing a softer-stop training distribution after the scheduled block. Dossiers work/ppo_gpu_05_causal_eval_03/carry_handoff.json and work/ppo_gpu_05_r3_bracket_03/.

reward_terms.name: approach
reward_terms.formula: New maximum of approach potential from housing-to-palm position, wrist angle and two intended pads near the housing.

reward_terms.name: lift
reward_terms.formula: New clearance potential of a gripped object, gated by opposed contact and referenced to 14 mm.

reward_terms.name: turn
reward_terms.formula: New maximum of the minimum of world blade-up progress and signed tilt reduction attributable to relative angle changes; paid only while continuously opposed, unsupported, and the contact digits have measured and commanded motion. Common wrist rotation cancels in the relative measurement.

reward_terms.name: carry
reward_terms.formula: New normalized reduction in goal distance during a blades-up carry with hand contact and no surface support.

reward_terms.name: seat
reward_terms.formula: New reduction in standing-height and tilt errors in the left zone while held.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: New gain in removal of hand contact and supported upright rest.

reward_terms.name: reference_wrist

reward_terms.name: reference_posture

reward_terms.name: reference_contact
reward_terms.formula: Progress-conditioned gain in object-frame contact agreement with reconstructed witnesses within a 9 mm free band.

reward_terms.name: bonus

simulator.name: MuJoCo

backends.training: MuJoCo Warp 3.17.0 on four L40S GPUs with 6,144 worlds per GPU, 2 ms physics and the station arm and hand at 100 Hz. Policy and sensor use 30 Hz.

simulator.training_reset: After a physical reset, refresh kinematics, contact and servo bias in a CUDA graph. Normal physics solves acceleration and constraints before integration. Audit structural capacity at each 2 ms substep and abort training if any GPU has truncated physics buffers.

scene.robot: Complete supplied Marvin–Wuji MJCF with official arm capsules and hand collision meshes, the parked left arm and the column and head stop volumes. Added table, pedestal and floor. The geometric station stops are evaluated directly on commanded and measured arm angles.
scene.object: Rounded convex 27 × 40 × 43 mm housing and two separated 6 × 1.5 × 15 mm blade boxes. Only the deployed white object is instantiated.

object_physical_properties.dominant_material: molded thermoplastic housing, plated metal blades

sources.mass_kg: Comparable Anker and Belkin 20 W adapters span 36–52 g (https://www.anker.com/products/b2348112-f0 and https://www.belkin.com/support-article/?articleNum=337529). Adopt 51 g for the larger housing.
sources.com_m: Homogeneous housing with heavier internal assembly offset 2 mm toward the back and two exterior brass blade cuboids.
sources.inertia_com_kgm2: Parallel-axis combination of housing and blade cuboids about the inferred combined COM.
sources.friction: Assumed effective coefficients for molded polymer against smooth laminate. Measure and randomize for robot deployment.
sources.restitution: Assumed 0.05, weak bounce of molded plastic on a rigid table; not identifiable from the clip.
sources.dominant_material: Appearance and construction class suggest a stiff molded thermoplastic with plated metal blades. Resin and alloy unobservable.
sources.size_m: TASK_CONFIG.md section 3 dimensions for the visually matching station adapter. Industrial design is consistent with the white Type A Apple 20 W USB-C form in https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mwvv3am/a/20w-usb-c-power-adapter. Brand identity is unconfirmed.

reference.source: Reconstruction version 6, right MANO wrist, plug_white world pose, phase annotations and object-frame contact witnesses.
reference.kinematic_replay: Align the opening blade direction to deployment yaw about the tabletop normal. Offset to the fixed start and gradually bring the endpoint to the center of the goal. Apply measured wrist rotations relative to the grasp wrist, which is anchored in the reachable robot hand frame from an opposed thumb–middle-finger pad solve. Re-solve the pad locations and the arm IK per frame. Choose the smallest collision-clear separation available at each frame. Keep the measured plug trajectory as an imposed pose for the kinematic audit.
reference.planned_reward_reference: Adapt the demonstrated object and wrist traces to each start and goal. Use object position, blade-axis rotation, wrist tracking, opposed-contact witnesses and ordered state-dependent progress. Keep the reconstruction in the reward and curriculum.

arm.controller: Public 100 Hz palm jump test, linear and rotational slew, box clamp, measured-joint seeded IK, coupled wrist and command speed clamps. Delayed position reference followed by an implicit, current-limited arm joint servo. Command and measured capsules are evaluated each tick.
arm.numerical_limit: The public reference integrator occasionally advances its feed-forward component past the IK boundary. Project the resulting joint reference to the same joint and coupled wrist box and clear outward velocity at a projected joint, consistent with the published lack of boundary overshoot. The unreachable-orientation test then passes.
arm.initialization_correction: Target replay r0034 showed that re-solving Cartesian IK at the placed palm during the ramp changed the arm null-space posture by 9.53 degrees. Joint hold reproduced all eight observed no-lift outcomes and reduced the median valid-state position residual from 334 mm to 53 mm. The remaining post-start Cartesian and arm servo law is the same.

hand.controller: Five ordered four-joint digits, 2 Hz first-order filter, 25 ms nominal fractional delay, torque-limited implicit position servo and compliant joint stops. Measured hand positions are delayed and receive 0.10 degree encoder noise.
hand.domain_randomization: Draw nominal or randomized strength, delay, friction, object inertia/mass, table edges and stop compliance. Nominal values are used in the frozen evaluation. The sampled distributions for each training run are recorded with its iteration.
hand.stop_distributions: Use .001–.010 rad sampled uniformly on randomized episodes, converted to max(.004, .006 × sqrt(compliance/.002)) for the constraint time constant while retaining the nominal damping ratio and deployed limits. The nominal compliant-stop setting remains .002 rad.

sensor.source: Published d2s_sensor.PoseSensor for delay, symmetry flips, noise, loss and validity/age. Contact-mesh-derived capsules approximate ego occlusion; sample 112 physical housing surface points and 12 blade face points. Recompute visibility at each physics-log tick.
sensor.encoder_delay: Normal 14 ms with 4.3 ms deviation, clipped to 4–29 ms and sampled on the logged 100 Hz trajectory.
sensor.training_backend: Published TorchPoseSensorBatch with the same default noise, delays and occlusion schedule, using the same 124 samples and arm or hand capsule rays in Warp. CPU and GPU use independently seeded noise streams.

initial_conditions.object: Uniform and independent xy offsets ±10 mm, yaw offset ±10 degrees about -90 degrees, state +X upward. Place with zero velocities on the table and verify support with the installed hold check. Use the published start IK and 1.5 s hand ramp.
initial_conditions.arm_ramp: Solve the package start once from the published reset joints. Keep those placed joint references for all 150 finger ramp ticks while gravity, finger dynamics, collisions and the pose sensor advance. No Cartesian IK iterations run the warm arm reference. At t=0, compare the first action with the measured palm. Local arm variation was at most 2.18e-5 rad over the ramp, and the final joint vector differs from target [redacted] by at most 1.63e-6 rad.
initial_conditions.training: GPU PPO uses the same simulated 1.5-second deployment ramp on each complete reset. Optional intermediate-state starts restore the position, velocity and hand preload of a mechanically settled pose. The fixture used during offline initialization is gone before the saved states. No controller commands enter the network training targets.

episode.termination: Published geometric and jump stops and invalid action or nonfinite state as policy failure. Finger and arm travel violations are logged without turning contact force into a stop.

station_check.departure: The finger-speed scenario warns on index MCP1 finite-difference peak near 10.1 rad/s compared with the model value 8.203. It remains below the filtered-step bound 22.117 rad/s and passes travel and station stop checks.

validation.fk: Compared MuJoCo palm FK to the arm model at reset (about 4 micrometres); station adapter passes published free-space, limit and stop checks.
validation.sensor_replay: Four independent 900-step lock-ramp candidate state logs reproduced contract-v3 sensor observations and all other checks with zero discrepancies.
validation.initial_hold: All 128 deployment evaluations retained the intended joint hold during the finger ramp and started the actor without a station stop. A full gate start check on the frozen v3 evaluator will verify the support convention.
validation.rollout_penetration: Retargeted reference maximum 0.992 mm. Exact r0106 fixed evaluation maximum 3.655 mm. See the 128-start nominal parity and the target-specific variations separately.
limitations: Mass, friction and inertia remain priors pending target calibration. Geometry treats blade holes and rear electrical recess as closed collision surfaces.

Capsules approximate partial occlusion by the glove. Finger pads are compliant contact surfaces over rigid links. The kinematic replay deviates up to 32 mm from the unconstrained palm placement and comes within 5 mm of the plug in 50 of 76 grasp frames. The reconstruction wrist and object remain the demonstration targets.

The target, nominal replay and corrected replay had median per-trial peak external torques of 89.95, 28.03 and 32.39 Nm. This is an estimated observation. Target finger excursions beyond the deployed travel allowance occurred in eight of eight; the corrected sent-command replay reproduced them in three of eight. Continue calibration using outcomes and uncertainty, not exact occluded trajectories.

parity.rollout_note: Full nominal 900-step episodes from the shared starts, exact station on the CPU side. No Warp capacity overflow.

throughput.description: Real matched station PPO using the v4 dynamics mixture and the same four-GPU implementation, profiled every update. The new mixture requires its own measured throughput.

validation.target_replay: R2 r0054 reproduced four lifts and seven measured finger-range violations with joint calibration at 0.1075 s arm delay and 0.010 rad compliant-stop parameter. Nominal yielded seven lifts and zero violations. The target had four visible lifts and eight measured violations. Preserve the remaining contact and pose uncertainty instead of identifying the target from a single fitted trajectory.
validation.dynamic_contact_diagnostic: Four matched task-feasibility command histories. GPU 4 lift, 2 turn, 1 carry, 0 place, versus CPU 4/4/3/3. No GPU stops or safety or capacity violations. The exact CPU judge remains the reference for learning carry into the low seated grasp.
validation.contract_in_training: All GPU worlds enforce finite actions/state, the station controller feedback and stops, measured finger and arm limits, and measured palm workspace and speed. One complete stream per rank feeds the installed ContractMonitor every controller row and policy step. The sampled episode ends when that monitor finds a problem. Full 900-step episodes are used throughout. The exact gate checks all policy episodes.

[redacted]_calibration.limitations: The target had eight visible lifts and eight measured excursions, with median peak 0.109 rad. The strongest tested replay peak medians were 0.041 on CPU and 0.038 on Warp. The new range covers estimated response uncertainty and is not a measurement of actual hardware compliance. All four variant runs, including the nominal one, had zero stops, zero carries and no structural overflow.

media.comparison_context: Reference kinematic replay and initial scene in the frozen v3 station frame. The new training uncertainty concerns compliant stops.

body.frozen_evaluator: Task suite v3 r0036 and feasibility r0037 retain the identical nominal exact CPU evaluator.
body.training_domain_parameters_description: Nominal 60%. The general uniform ranges apply on 25%. The remaining 15% also uses those uncertainty ranges, with arm delay and compliant-stop softness sampled from the measured subranges below.

training_target_stratum.evidence: R3 r0104 and records/sim5/[redacted]_calibration.json. CPU and Warp agree on median excursion increase over the old bracket and differ in excursion frequency and some hold outcomes.
training_target_stratum.sampling: Independent uniforms conditional on the same target stratum. General parameter ranges apply in a separate 25 percent of episodes. The other 60 percent use nominal dynamics.

gate_evidence.seen: r0106: both official failure montages show the plug in or near the grip at 0.46 s and separated flat on the table by 4.38 s. Round-three sent-command replay r0104 identifies an earlier finger travel change under load and supports broadening the training stop response.

body.reflection: The scheduled 38-minute causal continuation ended at 250,015,464 active interactions. The endpoint on 64 exact fixed starts scored 64 lifts, 27 turns, 16 carries, no placements or complete successes, nine rests, two hardware violations and one arm collision stop. Seed 924195 exceeded finger travel and stopped on arm collision. Seed 1080220 had an arm-travel violation. Local contract p99 0.263 ms. The earlier safe r0109 reached 29 carries and the fresh r0106 gate remains the accepted incumbent. No one in this block qualified for placement. Across 132 profiled updates on four L40S, end-to-end active rate was 108,953 steps per second inclusive, 110,216 after two updates. Zero structural overflows and no reported contract problems on 63 completed sampled audit streams. The full-rate dossier gives the timing breakdown. Use the r0106 optimizer and weights for an isolated broader target stop-compliance experiment.

body.text: Continue the accepted r0106 actor with its matched optimizer for an 18-minute R3 robustness comparison. Change only the stop-response randomization in the 15 percent target stratum from 0.008–0.010 to 0.012–0.038. CPU and GPU station checks are 13 pass and one explained warning each. The official 128-start nominal outcome comparison passes, with 53 versus 50 exact CPU and Warp carries on the r0106 actor. Under R3 sent commands the strongest 0.038 Warp variant reproduces seven of eight excursions and six lifts, and 0.022 reproduces five excursions and eight lifts. The target had eight lifts and eight excursions at larger peaks, so the branch spans uncertainty and is not a physical identification. The 250M-step line reached 29 safe carries at its highest exact checkpoint and no qualifying placement across all checkpoints. R0110 records sim5. Preserve full episode, r0036 exact CPU gate, causal turn reward, original 239-state bank, exploration and other physical ranges. Expect reduced ring/index approach excursions in the stronger paired bracket while preserving nominal carry. Profile all components of each update on CUDA 0–3. Keep the high-preseat curriculum and continuous-grip shaping as separate next experiments.

A candidate high-preseat curriculum is ready as a separate placement experiment. It adds 89 geometry-prepared opposed grips and 23 learner states collected from independent exact r0106 rollouts, preserving all 239 original states. The 96 collection-only starts had 96 lifts, 63 turns and 42 carries, zero placements and two hardware violations. Only safe held episodes contribute reset states. Each accepted start retained continuously opposed unsupported grip, upright angle and 10 mm clearance in the goal region for 0.20 s after restore, in nominal and the 0.1075 s and 0.022 rad R3 bracket. Every restored state contains its contact preload and physical velocity. Median height above standing centre is 137 mm for prepared starts and 133 mm for learner starts, versus 13 mm in the 19 legacy preseat starts. body.text: R3 timing and a narrow ring action intervention. At the seven largest ring MCP2 excursion timestamps, nominal CPU replay measured about minus 0.298 to minus 0.306 rad. The target ring measured minus 0.346 to minus 0.429. The contemporaneous sent ring target was inside the limits and moving upward. Trial 6 instead peaks on index MCP1. The stored commands leading into peak are in work/[redacted]/timing_finger_excursion.json. In the R3 bracket a diagnostic changed only the lower ring target bound in the first six seconds, preserving the recorded other commands. Baseline minus 0.300 gives 8/8 excursions, and floors minus 0.270, minus 0.240, minus 0.210 and minus 0.170 give 7/8, 8/8, 8/8 and 8/8 respectively. All cases lifted. There is no material safety gain from a simple ring target floor. It remains an offline test, with the actor, station limits and active training preserved. See work/[redacted]/ring_action_floor.json.

body.reflection: The wider-stop comparison ended at 116,632,297 active interactions. Its exact 64-start endpoint has 62 lifts, 26 turns, 18 carries, zero placements or complete success, two hardware violations and one stop. Final rest on 22 and contract p99 0.282 ms. On paired R3-bracket starts it gave 16 lifts, six turns, five carries, 14 hardware violations and one stop. The earlier 8/16 excursion count was temporary and neither complete execution nor other stages improved against the accepted parent. Whole-run active throughput 107,598 inclusive and 110,301 after two warm-up updates across all four L40S, with every update profiled and no buffer overflow. The exact sampled training monitor reported one joint position beyond the 0.05 rad contract tolerance at 2.30 s on rank 3, and stopped that episode after 69 policy steps. The batched travel limit was active at the same policy boundary. The wider-stop run has no package selected for gate. Continue the accepted r0106 lineage in a separate high-preseat curriculum comparison.

body.text: Test high-preseat starts as an isolated curriculum change from r0106, using the matched optimizer and sim4 physical range that produced that incumbent. The broader sim5 stop response is recorded separately and did not yield a durable reduction in bracket violations or a stronger nominal package. Keep the causal reward, policy architecture, exploration, stage weights, episode length and four-GPU configuration. The only learning change against r0106 is work/training_reset_pool_early_seat.json, adding 112 physically verified phase-4 starts from r0113 to the original 239. It includes 23 actual learner handoffs with velocities from independent collection-only starts. Expect better advancement from held high states and the first ordered supported seats on full starts. Train 26 minutes with three-view fixed exact evaluation at approximately 35M-step intervals and all component timings at each update. The active r0106 failure montages were opened and show separation before placement, with the corresponding 25-run handoff logs showing no support before release. No demonstration actions are copied.

A prospective lowering term was checked offline on 12 held learner states and 12 geometry-prepared high preseat states. A 0.100 m height scale delivers median early credit 2.46 and 2.21 during the first 0.60 s of controlled lowering, versus zero at the current 0.025 m scale. Requiring object-height improvement with at least half that descent at the measured palm, uninterrupted hand contact inside the zone and active downward target change left zero reward on all 24 fixed-target controls. The same wide potential without the target-causality condition paid on 18/24 fixed controls. Random wrist perturbations caused limited real descent, with proposed median early credit 0.46 and 0.16 and no seats. The lowering controls produced one supported seat on the learner cases and eight on the prepared cases, with zero hardware violations or stops. These are physical and reward diagnostics, not task policy episodes. This term could be tried as one reward change after the current high-preseat curriculum comparison. Log and code work/seat_height_reward_probe.json and work/probe_seat_height_reward.py.

body.text: Operator R3 contact diagnosis received around 23:18 UTC. The station view shows the middle finger spreading into the ring before grasp. Seven trials peak on lower ring MCP2 while middle MCP2 sits at its lower stop; the sent ring target has already moved in the opposite direction. The recent package starts middle MCP2 at -0.294 rad. The supplied scene excludes these finger-link pairs, so the earlier compliant-stop sweeps lack the suspected load source. Test explicit middle–ring contacts in an isolated training scene and compare against all eight already archived R3 command streams, including the initial ramp. Compare start-pose clearances and whether an interior middle spread prevents contact. The frozen task evaluator and physical limits remain the comparison reference.

body.text: The R3 finger-contact mechanism is geometrically plausible. The frozen scene excludes all 16 middle–ring links, while the hulls at the commanded start overlap by 7.29 mm. At the recorded encoder configuration around policy time 0.033 s the same nearest pair overlaps by 6.80 mm. The deepest pair is at the distal links. With the ring MCP2 at zero and other start joints fixed, middle MCP2 -0.15 gives 1.58 mm bare hull clearance and -0.10 gives 1.75 mm. An isolated copy enables those 16 contacts at the published glove margins. Contact constraints are active during the ramp and early policy. They change the trial 0 effective middle MCP2 at t=0 from -0.274 to -0.162 rad, versus target -0.270. With physical contact, 0.1075 s delay and nominal stop response, all eight sent streams lift and four turn, with zero measured excursions. Their first-half-second ring peak excess is 0.002–0.008 rad, much smaller than the target. The hulls are therefore useful clearance evidence and the simple contact variant does not match target force or encoder dynamics. A paired exact and contact-enabled closed-loop start sweep is running for middle angles -0.294, -0.150 and -0.100. The original simulation and evaluator are frozen. Dossiers work/finger_contact/measured_geometry.json and work/finger_contact/hulls_active/diagnostics.json.

body.text: Paired 16-start MCP2 ablation with r0106 weights. On the frozen CPU scene both interior start angles remove predicted bare-hull overlap in all 16 pregrasp trajectories, versus overlap in all 16 under the old start. Median worst early gap changes from -6.86 mm to +1.67 mm at -0.150 and +1.74 mm at -0.100. Nominal lift/turn/carry is 16/9/6 old, 16/10/6 at -0.150, 16/9/7 at -0.100, with zero violations or stops. In the contact-enabled and arm-delay .1075 s diagnostic, the corresponding stage counts are 16/10/1, 16/9/3 and 16/7/3, with one, one and zero measured violations. The corrected contact scene itself forces the old spread inward during the ramp, so its lack of overlap there cannot stand in for target safety. Select -0.100 as the local more interior start candidate, check it on all 64 exact fixed starts, and preserve the active curriculum run. This is not a target verification. Evidence work/finger_contact/pose_sweep/scored.json.

The -0.100 middle MCP2 diagnostic package with unchanged r0106 weights passes contract v3 locally at p99 0.270 ms. The full nominal 64-start evaluation gives 64 lifts, 39 qualifying turns, 23 carries, 12 final rests and no hardware violations or stops. The original r0106 pose has 64, 37, 25 and 19 respectively on the same starts. Both have zero seats and successes. The projection to an interior start removes the measured geometric overlap in the paired 16-start check while retaining the bulk of learned performance. Keep it as the next experiment baseline pending a fresh gate and target. Source work/finger_contact/inner100_exact64/scored.json. Causal lowering term is prepared but not active. A CPU tensor test passed real-lowering and zero-credit controls for fixed targets, empty wrist motion, gravity-only object motion, prior goal exit and intervening contact break. The full Warp paired reward check will run once the current curriculum block ends.

body.text: Warp validation of the proposed causal lowering term passed. On 24 held start states with fixed targets, every height credit is zero, median combined seating progress zero, no seat or stop. In 24 controlled descent rollouts, median new height credit is 2.406 over the first 0.60 s and 5.093 total, with 11 supported physical seats and zero stops or hardware violations. In 24 random wrist walks, the median early height credit is 0.172, later 0.335, with no seats or faults. These small random rewards require physical lowering of the held object. CPU controls previously gave zero on all holds and larger purposeful than random descent. The implementation latches hand contact across 100 Hz controller ticks, requires a causal descending target and measured palm displacement, and starts the new potential at its measured entry value. This is a separate preparation test. The current curriculum study does not use the new term. Evidence work/seat_lowering_warp_probe.json. The full 64-start -0.100 pose ablation also has zero predicted pregrasp bare-hull overlaps (minimum 1.739 mm), per work/finger_contact/inner100_exact64/pregrasp_clearance.json.

body.text: Compare the causal seat lowering reward against the measured -0.100 rad middle MCP2 starting configuration with the same r0106 weights and optimizer. The start change is independently evaluated in r0126 and r0127, preserving 23 of 64 nominal carries and eliminating bare hull overlap across all 64 pregrasp logs. Sim4 nominal and physical randomization settings, original 239-state bank, causal turn reward, action noise, rest and seating criteria, and full 900-step length remain those of the accepted lineage. The reward-only intervention relative to that neutral-start baseline broadens seat height scale from 25 to 100 mm and pays for lowering a held plug inside the goal only with corroborating wrist descent and downward targeting. Contact is latched across 100 Hz ticks. The baseline begins at measured entry value. CPU and Warp hold controls earn zero new height reward and commanded physical lowers earn early credit (r0120 and r0129). Train 26 minutes on all four GPUs, with every update profiled and 35M interaction checkpoint spacing. Expect the first ordered supported placements while preserving upstream stages and clearance. Latest r0106 gate montages show separation before support. R3 self-contact remains separate diagnostic physics, with all task gates on the frozen CPU model.

At each of the 25 qualifying r0106 carries on the 64 fixed starts, the actual held-object position and commanded wrist target rose after entering the goal. Over the first 0.30 s, or until any earlier grip loss, median changes are +53.1 mm commanded palm, +31.4 mm measured palm and +35.2 mm plug body centre. All 25 leave the goal footprint before disconnecting. The seat failure is observable as continued lift and transport after goal entry. The causal lowering experiment rewards a real alternative effect while the plug remains held over the goal. body.text: Paired exact CPU preseat exploration probe. On 24 physically stable elevated states split between learner handoffs and prepared grips, the same bounded, diagnostic-only 3.5 mm per step downward target and fixed finger mean produced eight supported upright seats, median held time 1.633 s and median in-zone lowering 124.4 mm without added noise. The same seeded Gaussian draws at latent sigma 0.35, 0.65 and 2.226 produced two, one and one seats, held time 0.833, 0.833 and 0.583 s and lowering 74.3, 29.7 and 14.8 mm. The 0.35 condition had one stop and one excursion. No actions are training data. This tests the sensitivity of descent under the actual action bounds, separately from what the learner chooses. Test fixed latent sigma 0.35 against the saturated 2.226 exploration with identical r0106 actor and optimizer, -0.100 middle MCP2 start, causal lowering reward, original curriculum, nominal and randomized station, seed 4848292 and all four GPUs. First compare 64 exact trials at roughly 35M and 70M steps. Expect sustained support and a longer grip with similar or better carry; judge exact task stages and faults. Exact paired 64-start deployment evaluation: 64 lifts, 29 verified turns, 17 carries, zero placements and successes, one hardware violation (finger travel 0.020200 rad over limit, seed 986605) and zero stops. Fourteen final rests. Contract p99 0.474 ms. The safe-start parent gave 64 lifts, 39 turns, 23 carries, zero violations and 12 rests. The first lowering checkpoint got closer to support than this one. All 17 left the original grip before support, 10 laterally left the goal first and none had a valid pose at the handoff. Median minimum held clearance 115 mm and median held time 0.36 s. Over the first 0.30 s after goal entry, median measured wrist rose 54 mm and held body rose 57 mm. Two later upright support contacts followed grip loss. Continue the matched run and compare later checkpoints. A paired controlled-descent diagnostic r0134 measures substantially longer hold and more lowering at sigma 0.35 than at the current saturated 2.226. It motivates the next all-four-GPU PPO comparison, starting from the same actor and training reward with exploration fixed to 0.35.

The adapted reference from reconstruction r0009 enters at y=0.022 m with 17.6 mm clearance near frame 149 and descends from 33.7 mm at y=-0.048 m near frame 139. The safe-start actor median entry is about 130 mm and lateral velocity about +0.51 m/s, and measured clearance increases on earlier approaches (-0.10 through goal). Exact paired diagnostic work/lower_transfer_probe.json uses the same 32 physically validated early grips and same slow planar target with fixed fingers. Both level and descending transfer reach the zone upright in 22/32. The level condition reaches zero upright supported seats, lowering reaches ten (two from learner and eight prepared), with one collision stop and no excursions. Median body centre height above standing at entry in the learner grips drops from 88 to 34 mm. The test holds the grasp and does not verify the final release. These controller actions are diagnostic only. If reduced exploration does not address placement, test an independently validated height-progress term during upright carry using the demonstration height as a forward-reachable reference before the goal edge.

Exact fixed 64-start evaluation gives 64 lifts, 30 turns, 16 carries, no qualifying place or success, zero hardware violations and zero stops, 14 final rests. Contract p99 0.267 ms. The same-start parent gives 64 lifts, 39 turns and 23 carries, zero placements or faults. Median entry clearance now 104.6 mm and minimum held clearance 90.9 mm, compared with 130.2 and 110 mm for the parent. Median held time 0.705 s. All 16 still separate prior to support and have no valid object pose at entry. Eleven exit the goal before grip loss. Median body movement over the first 0.30 s after entry is still 44 mm upward. Reconstructed entry clearance is about 18 mm. Continued reduction in attained height is promising for the proximal metric only. The next isolated run compares 0.35 fixed latent exploration with all other conditions matched. r0136 gives paired diagnostic evidence for extending the lowering incentive to the approach to the goal if placement stays flat.

body.text: Middle–ring geometry extended through the first opposed contact and 450 ms. The original start predicts bare mesh overlap before opposition in 64/64 for r0106. With the -0.100 rad middle start, zero of 64 have bare overlap before opposed contact at the parent, first lowering checkpoint and third lowering checkpoint. Positive minimum to opposition is 1.728 mm at the parent and 1.739 mm at both trained checkpoints. Through the entire first 450 ms, overlap returns in 1, 4 and 10 of 64, respectively, all after opposed contact. Earliest ages are 0.44, 0.45 and 0.42 s, distinct from early [redacted] station observations at 0.30–0.33 s. The training station has the supplied exclusions and does not generate these forces. Use this as a geometry risk indicator when selecting the next package and compare actual joint excursions on its target trial. Data in each fixed evaluation folder pregrasp_clearance.json.

The occluded high handoff is geometrically observable on the tested held rollouts. In the 23 exact carries at the safer start, the stale pose has median planar and vertical errors 193 and 112 mm around goal entry. A leave-one-episode-out constant object offset in the delayed observed palm frame gives 5.8 and 10.7 mm median errors, with p90 11.4 and 17.2 mm, on the same 241 samples. The third lowering checkpoint gives 9.0 and 13.0 mm median and 13.3 and 16.6 mm p90, across 16 carries. Selection uses the true held and upright labels offline. It does not prove that the policy can recognise the held phase or detect support from those observations. The regression is a diagnostic only, with no addition to the package or weights. This supports trying earlier lowering before changing observation history. See the occluded_carry_geometry.json reports in each evaluation.
